issues.failure_explanation: The expression $tf(x)+(1-t)g(x)\bmod 1$ has no meaning without choosing real lifts of the circle values $f(x),g(x)$; the proof lifts $f$ and $g$ along each loop $\gamma\in\mathcal{P}$ separately (the displayed computation uses lift differences $f_\gamma(1-0)-f_\gamma(0)=\omega(f_\gamma)$). The only check performed, \eqref{well-def}, shows that within each single loop the interpolated lift closes up (using $\omega(f_\gamma)=\omega(g_\gamma)$); it never checks that the values assigned at a point lying on two loops (e.g., a junction vertex shared by $\gamma_0,\gamma_1,\gamma_2$) agree. Independent per-loop lift choices differ by integer constants, and changing the lift of $f$ on one loop by $1$ changes $F(\tau,x)$ by $\tau\bmod 1\neq 0$ for $\tau\in(0,1)$, so $F$ is not single-valued on $\bigcup\mathcal{P}$ unless lifts are chosen coherently. A coherent choice exists exactly when $f-g$ admits a global lift $G\to\R$ (equivalently, a map with zero winding on every $\partial T_w$ is nullhomotopic) — essentially the content of the direction being proved — and this is never established. Hence the inference that $F$ is a (uniformly continuous) function on $\mathcal{P}\times[0,1]$, and its extension to $G\times[0,1]$, is unsupported.

failure_location.quote:
Thus, $F$ is a uniformly continuous function on $\mathcal{P}\times [0,1]$. Since $\mathcal{P}$
    is dense in $G$ there is a unique continuous extension of $F$ to $G\times [0,1].$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove the missing lifting lemma (a continuous $h:G\to\T$ with zero winding on every cell boundary $\partial T_w$ is nullhomotopic, e.g., via the retractions $r_n:G\to\Gamma_n$ with $r_n\to\mathrm{id}$ uniformly, so $h\simeq h\circ r_n$ and $h\circ r_n$ is nullhomotopic on the finite graph $\Gamma_n$), then define the homotopy as $F(t,x)=g(x)+t\tilde h(x)\bmod 1$ with $\tilde h$ the global lift of $f-g$; alternatively construct the homotopy inductively on the graphs $\Gamma_n$.
issues.overall_effect: The 'if' direction of Theorem 2.1 — that the degree vector \eqref{w-vector} determines the homotopy class of a map $G\to\T$ (the classification invoked in the Introduction and underlying the prescription \eqref{homotopy-c} of a homotopy class) — is unproved as written.
issues.title: Homotopy formula in Theorem 2.1 is not shown to be well defined on G
issues.why_classification: The statement is true and no advertised conclusion is lost, but the missing step is a genuine new (though contained) lemma — the global lifting criterion on SG — not a routine local edit; the proof strategy and all claims survive its insertion.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
\hat H=\{ f\in C(G,\T):\; \p_{v_1v_2} f=\delta_1, \; \p_{v_2v_3} f=\delta_2,\; 
    \p_{v_3v_1} f=\rho_0-\delta_1-\delta_2\}

issues.failure_explanation: The uniqueness half of Theorem 2.3 is justified only by the Section 6 claim that $\hat f^\ast$ is the unique minimizer of $\hat\cE$ over $\hat H$. But the comparison identity $\hat\cE_m(\hat g)=E[\Gamma_m^0](\tilde g)$ is available only for competitors $\hat g$ that lift to the cut graph, i.e., have zero winding around every subloop $\partial T_w$, $|w|\ge 1$; Lemma 5.1 compares only such real-valued competitors in $H_m^0$. The class $\hat H$ imposes only the boundary lift conditions \eqref{bc-hm} and contains continuous maps with the same boundary data but nonzero subloop windings (the higher-order construction of Section 7 produces such HMs), for which no energy comparison is given (an unwinding/strict-energy-gap argument is needed and is absent). In addition, Theorem 2.3 asserts uniqueness among harmonic maps, and the paper never argues that an arbitrary HM with the data is the energy minimizer (that its lift is discrete-harmonic with the $H_m^0$ constraints and the coupled Kirchhoff condition at the cut, hence equals $f_m^0$ on the dense set).

failure_location.quote:
This combined with Lemma~\ref{lem.minimizer} implies that $\hat f^\ast$ is a unique minimizer of 
$\hat \cE$ in $\hat H$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the standard Dirichlet-principle argument: any HM $f$ with data \eqref{bc-hm} and degree \eqref{homotopy-c} lifts to a real-valued harmonic function on the covering whose restrictions to $V_m^0$ satisfy the $H_m^0$ constraints, hence coincide with the unique minimizer $f_m^0$, so $f=\hat f^\ast$ by density; and/or show that any element of $\hat H$ with an extra subloop winding has strictly larger $\hat\cE$ (a unit jump across a cut raises the minimum energy by a fixed positive amount).
issues.overall_effect: The uniqueness assertion of the main result for the SG (Theorem 2.3) lacks a complete argument; the variational characterization in Section 6 is proved only among liftable competitors. Existence is unaffected.
issues.title: Uniqueness in Theorem 2.3 not established against competitors with extra loop windings
issues.why_classification: The statement is true and the missing pieces are short, standard arguments (lifting plus Dirichlet principle, or a contained unwinding estimate) that preserve every claim and the advertised scope; the gap is a concrete unhandled competitor class, not a wish for more exposition.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Thus, $\mathbf{f}^\ast|_{V_m^k}$ is $\Gamma^k_m$-harmonic and
it remains to check that $\mathbf{f}^\ast|_{\tilde V_m}$ satisfies the 
discrete Laplace equation at $z_{\pm}^k$.

issues.failure_explanation: \eqref{G-harmonic} quantifies over all nodes of $\tilde V_m$, including the sheet boundary vertices $v_1^k,v_2^k,v_3^k$, whose values are prescribed data \eqref{def-H} and which are not identified with any other node of the covering graph. The discrete Laplace equation fails there in general: for $\rho_0=1$, $\delta_1=\delta_2=0$, formula \eqref{Hext} gives $f^\ast(x)=-1/10$, $f^\ast(z_-^0)=-1/2$, so $\Delta_1\mathbf{f}^\ast(v_1^0)=(-1/10)+(-1/2)=-3/5\neq 0$ (and $\Delta_1\mathbf{f}^\ast(v_3^0)=3/5$). The proof itself establishes the equation only at interior nodes and at the glued cut points $z_\pm^k$, which is all that is true and all that is later used.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the quantifier in \eqref{G-harmonic} to interior nodes, i.e., exclude the pinned vertices $V_0^k$ (e.g., $\forall x\in\tilde V_m\setminus\bigcup_k V_0^k$), consistent with the definition of $\Gamma_m$-harmonicity and with the proof.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed claim of Theorem 5.1 is false as written; the valid content is harmonicity at the nodes of $\tilde V_m$ other than the pinned boundary vertices $V_0^k$.
issues.title: Equation (5.6) asserts the discrete Laplace equation at pinned boundary vertices, where it fails
issues.why_classification: A single forced local correction (exclude the boundary vertices) makes the statement true, and every downstream use (the minimization argument of Section 6) needs only the interior and cut-point equation, so no claim or guarantee is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The jump conditions used throughout — $f(z_+^k)=f(z_-^k)+\rho_0$ \eqref{def-H}, $f(v_{c_+(w)}^k)=f(v_{c_-(w)}^k)+\rho_{\ell(w)}$ in Section 7, and $f((v_i^{(m)})_{c+}^k)=f((v_i^{(m)})_{c-}^k)+\rho_i$ in the proof of Theorem 8.1 — together with the $k$-periodic extension $\mathbf f(x,k)=f(x)+k$ \eqref{k-period}, force the identification $v_{c_+}^k\simeq v_{c_-}^{k+\rho}$ for $\mathbf f$ to be well defined (and continuous) on the glued space; this is the convention used correctly in \eqref{identify} and in Appendix item 2(c). The displayed formulas in \eqref{eq:sg_gen_cuts}, in the proof of Theorem 8.1, and in Appendix item 1 instead identify $v_{c_-}^k$ with $v_{c_+}^{k+\rho}$, and \eqref{eq:sg_gen_cuts} moreover shifts by the loop index $\ell(w)$ rather than by the prescribed winding number $\rho_{\ell(w)}$. Read literally, the two values of $\mathbf f$ at a glued pair differ by $2\rho$ (respectively by $\rho_{\ell(w)}+\ell(w)$), so the purported harmonic function on the covering space is not well defined and the covering does not encode the prescribed windings.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Write the identifications in the consistent direction, $v_{c_+(w)}^k\simeq v_{c_-(w)}^{k+\rho_{\ell(w)}}$ (and $z_+^k\simeq z_-^{k+\rho_0}$ in Appendix item 1, $(v_i^{(m)})_{c_+}^k\simeq (v_i^{(m)})_{c_-}^{k+\rho_i}$ in the proof of Theorem 8.1), matching \eqref{identify}, Appendix item 2(c), and all jump conditions.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the higher-order covering-space construction of Section 7 (hence the general-degree case of Theorem 2.3), the covering built in the proof of Theorem 8.1, and the level-0 gluing in Appendix item 1 are each internally inconsistent with their own jump conditions.
issues.title: Sheet-identification formulas glue the wrong sides/sheets relative to the jump conditions
issues.why_classification: The consistent convention is explicitly present in the paper (\eqref{identify}, every jump condition, Appendix item 2(c)), and the repair is a local rewrite of the displayed formulas with no change to any result; it exceeds a pure typo because the same reversal recurs in three displays and \eqref{eq:sg_gen_cuts} needs two coordinated changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
At step $m>0$, we have $0<|w|=m\le N$ and choose cut point $\xi_w^k\in V^k_{m+1}$ such that
it belongs to the boundary of the corresponding $m$-cell, $\partial T_{(w_1,w_2,\dots, w_m)}$

issues.failure_explanation: In Appendix item 2 the cut point $x_w$ (resp. $y_w,z_w$) lies on the boundary of the child cell $T_{w1}$ (resp. $T_{w2},T_{w3}$) and carries the shift $\rho_{\ell(w1)}$ (resp. $\rho_{\ell(w2)},\rho_{\ell(w3)}$), so for $|w|=m$ item 2 produces the cuts for loops of level $m+1$. With the stated range $1\le m\le N$ the recipe therefore covers loop levels $2,\dots,N+1$: the cuts for the level-1 loops $\partial T_1,\partial T_2,\partial T_3$ — the case $m=0$, $w=\emptyset$, with shifts $\rho_1,\rho_2,\rho_3$ — are never made, while unnecessary (zero-shift, hence harmless) cuts at level $N+1$ are included. Following the recipe literally, the prescribed windings $\rho_1,\rho_2,\rho_3$ are not implemented, so the appendix's explicit formulas do not construct the covering space needed for the second-order HMs they are stated to serve (Section 7 refers to the appendix for exactly these cut points).

failure_location.quote: In addition, for every $1\le m\le N$ and $w\in S^m$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the range in item 2 to $0\le m\le N-1$ (with $S^0=\{\emptyset\}$), so that cuts are produced for loop levels $1,\dots,N$; the formulas in (a)–(c) are already correct for $m=0$.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit cut-point construction in Appendix A builds the wrong set of cuts for HMs with nonzero level-1 winding numbers; the general construction in Section 7 is correct and unaffected.
issues.title: Appendix cut-point recipe omits the cuts for the level-1 loops
issues.why_classification: The repair is a small range correction to an illustrative recipe whose formulas are already correct, and the correct general prescription exists in Section 7, so nothing substantive is lost; but as written the recipe constructs the wrong cut set, which is a construction error rather than a single misprinted symbol.
